title: Google put AI chips in orbit

beats: Google just launched four AI chips into orbit.
Real hardware. Circling Earth right now.
October first. A SpaceX rocket, out of California.
Sixty-one minutes after liftoff, the satellite was loose in orbit.
Google says it called home, and everything works.
Why bother? Because AI is running out of power.
The same week, Amazon locked up six hundred ninety megawatts of nuclear power. For twenty years.
Space has a trick.
In the right orbit, the sun almost never sets. So solar panels can run nearly nonstop.
The satellite is the size of a refrigerator.
Four chips. About one kilowatt of solar power.
It's small on purpose. This is a test.
Before launch, Google blasted the chips with a proton beam, while they ran AI.

The real plan is bigger. Eighty-one satellites, in a one-kilometer cluster, six hundred fifty kilometers up.
